title: How a C# program works
intro: C# is a compiled language that runs on the Common Language Runtime (CLR), not in a JavaScript engine. This module walks you through the full path from writing code to running it — including project setup, namespaces, where execution starts, and quick single-file scripts.

overviewDiagram.title: Module overview: from source to running app
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Write C# source] --> B[Project file or #: directives]
  B --> C[Roslyn compiles to IL]
  C --> D[CLR loads assembly]
  D --> E[Entry point: Main or top-level]
  E --> F[JIT or AOT to machine code]
  F --> G[Program runs]

conceptCards.title: C# vs JavaScript/TypeScript
conceptCards.summary: C# types survive compile into Intermediate Language (IL). TypeScript types disappear before run time. Different hosts: CLR vs V8.
conceptCards.example: An int in C# is still Int32 at run time; a TS number becomes a JavaScript number.

conceptCards.title: Compilation pipeline
conceptCards.summary: Source → Roslyn → IL → tiered JIT or R2R or Native AOT → CPU code.
conceptCards.example: Tier 0 quick JIT, then optimized tier for hot methods

conceptCards.title: Project and language version
conceptCards.summary: The .csproj sets Target Framework Moniker (TFM), language version, and implicit usings. Pin TFM, not latest.
conceptCards.example: net10.0 defaults to C# 14 with auto-generated global usings.

conceptCards.title: Namespaces and usings
conceptCards.summary: Namespaces organize type names. Using statements shorten names at compile time — they do not load packages.
conceptCards.example: using System.Text.Json; is a name shortcut, not an npm import.

conceptCards.title: Entry points
conceptCards.summary: Every executable has exactly one start: classic static Main or top-level statements in one file.
conceptCards.example: dotnet new console creates a file with top-level statements and a hidden Main.

conceptCards.title: File-based apps
conceptCards.summary: C# 14 #: directives. PublishAot or ReadyToRun on publish. Convert to project when it grows.
